questions.q: Which of these is something XGBoost adds beyond the plain boosting loop from Lesson 1?
options: Regularization penalties on tree complexity
It removes the need for any training data
It replaces trees with linear regression
It guarantees no overfitting
questions.explain: XGBoost's objective penalizes complexity through reg_lambda, reg_alpha and gamma. It does not guarantee against overfitting.

questions.q: How does XGBoost handle missing values in the input features?
options: It refuses to train unless every value is filled in
It drops every row that contains a blank
It learns at each split which direction rows with a missing value should go
It always replaces blanks with zero
questions.explain: Sparsity-aware split finding lets XGBoost learn a default direction for missing values, so imputation is optional.

questions.q: Why do we use three splits (train, validation, test) when using early stopping?
options: Three splits make the model train faster
The validation set guides when to stop, so the test set remains an unbiased final check
XGBoost requires exactly three data frames
The test set is used to choose the number of trees
questions.explain: If you used the test set to pick the stopping round, the test score would be optimistically biased.

questions.q: In the lesson, early_stopping_rounds=30 means what?
options: Train exactly 30 trees
Stop after 30 seconds
Use only 30 features
Stop if the validation metric has not improved for 30 rounds
questions.explain: Training halts once the validation metric fails to improve for 30 consecutive rounds, and the best round is kept.

questions.q: What is the right way to read model.feature_importances_?
options: As proof that a feature causes churn
As a clue about which features the trees used, which can mislead when features are correlated
As the exact effect of each feature in percentage points
As a measure of the test-set accuracy
questions.explain: Importances describe model usage, not causation, and correlated features can split or steal credit from each other.
